clue.text: Spooner's springtime song and dance is renowned

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two words wanted here trade their first sounds

blocks.note: May is a spring month; it lends its opening sound to the second word and takes the other's
a song and dance is a fuss; with the opening sounds swapped it ends the answer

explanation.surface: A seasonal number with dancing has become well known.
explanation.walkthrough: MAY FUSS with its first sounds swapped becomes FAY MUSS, said together as FAMOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone famous is widely known and celebrated, which is what renowned means: a straight synonym.

clue.text: Small, slim and chaste

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
without a pot belly, so slim

explanation.surface: A description of a petite, slender and virtuous person.
explanation.walkthrough: A pot is a paunch, so someone potless has no belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotless means without moral stain, as a chaste and pure character is.

clue.text: WC in French hospital fascinates idiot cleaner

indicators.note: one thing set in another sits inside it, so the toilet goes within the French abbreviation
to fascinate is read as to hold captive, so the earlier letters wrap round the fool

blocks.note: a loo is a WC, a toilet
Fr is the abbreviation for French
H is the map symbol for a hospital
a clot is a fool

explanation.surface: A French hospital toilet is so captivating that a simpleton is cleaning it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fascinates' is read literally as 'holds captive': the first two pieces together wrap round the fool. H is the map symbol for a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A floorcloth is a rag for washing floors, an example of a cleaning implement.

clue.text: Chairmen in prime positions progress rapidly

indicators.note: prime positions are the second, third, fifth and seventh places, so only letters standing there are kept

blocks.note: the letters at positions two, three, five and seven of the word

explanation.surface: Company chairs in the top jobs climb quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: Prime here is mathematical: 2, 3, 5 and 7 are prime numbers, not top-ranking posts.
explanation.definitionFit: To hare is to run very fast, like the animal, so it is a verb for moving quickly.

clue.text: Moderate willing to support betrayal after head's departure

indicators.note: the head departing means the first letter of the word for treachery is dropped
in a down entry, a piece that supports another sits beneath it

blocks.note: treason is betrayal of one's country
able here means willing and capable

explanation.surface: A centrist will back treachery once the leader has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: TREASON loses its first letter to give REASON, and ABLE goes under it in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasonable means fair and not extreme, as in a moderate price: an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Destroy one god and another when half-cut

indicators.note: half-cut, besides meaning drunk, says half of the second god's name is removed

blocks.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god
Zeus is the chief Greek god

explanation.surface: Two drunken deities wreck the place.
explanation.walkthrough: Half-cut is British slang for tipsy; here it trims ZEUS to ZE.
explanation.definitionFit: To raze a building is to level it completely, a synonym for destroying it.

clue.text: Some of us lunch for our convenience

definitions.note: a noun phrase for a women's toilet, spoken by the women themselves

blocks.note: first meaning: '... who lunch' is the phrase for women of leisure meeting over long meals
second meaning: the women's public toilet, a convenience being British for a public loo

explanation.surface: A group of women explain their lunches are arranged to suit themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: The speaker is a woman, so 'us' and 'our' point to women; a public convenience is a British euphemism for a public toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'ladies who lunch' names such women, and the Ladies is the usual sign on a women's toilet.

clue.text: Build up cropped hair from the back, causing further stress

indicators.note: something cropped has been cut short, so the last letter of the verb for building goes
read from the back means the word for hair is spelt from its last letter to its first

blocks.note: to rear is to raise or build up
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A hairdresser shapes a short back cut, putting more strain on the client.
explanation.walkthrough: REAR cropped gives REA; TRESS reversed gives SSERT.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassert a point is to insist on it again, laying further emphasis or stress on it.

clue.text: Designation of court application the Spanish delayed

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective naming a kind of court

blocks.note: app is short for application
el is Spanish for the
late means delayed

explanation.surface: A court's paperwork with a Spanish name was filed late.
explanation.definitionFit: An appellate court hears appeals, so the word is the label describing that kind of tribunal.

clue.text: Some cheek a warder on returning to stir

definitions.note: a verb: to rouse from sleep

indicators.note: some of a phrase means only a part of its letters is taken
something returning goes back the way it came, so the letters run right to left

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling the three words

explanation.surface: A prison guard back on duty gets some cheeky backchat from the inmates.
explanation.definitionFit: To awake is to stir from sleep, used as a verb in the same way.

clue.text: Overrule cryptic indication of veto

blocks.note: surface reading: a hint at blocking a decision
setter's reading: veto is a jumble of a four-letter ballot word, signalled by an anagram signal such as 'out'

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as OUT plus VOTE: in crossword style that instructs you to rearrange VOTE, which gives VETO.
explanation.definitionFit: To outvote people is to defeat them by a majority, overriding their decision.

clue.text: Sort of glasses worn by Irene on vacation

indicators.note: vacating a name empties it, so only its outside letters remain
glasses worn sit around the face, so the eyewear word encloses the woman's remnant

blocks.note: specs is short for spectacles
the first and last letters of the name

explanation.surface: A holidaying woman puts on a particular style of spectacles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On vacation' is the crossword convention for emptying a word of its middle letters, leaving only the ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A species is a kind or type, as in 'a species of fraud': a sort.

clue.text: Girl should, on releasing hold, thrive at last

indicators.note: releasing lets something go, so the letters of the grip word are dropped from the modal verb
at last points to the final letter of the verb for flourishing

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, the letters removed
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Advice that a girl ought to flourish once freed from someone's grip.
explanation.walkthrough: SHOULD minus the letters of HOLD leaves SU; add E.
explanation.definitionFit: Sue is a girl's name, the short form of Susan, so it stands for any girl.

clue.text: Most of CNN a tad upset about word processing facility

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its final letter
about suggests letters being moved around, so the fodder is rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, then shortened
taken as written

explanation.surface: The news channel is somewhat disturbed by a feature of editing software.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; 'about' does that job.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut-and-paste is the editing function for moving text in a document.

clue.text: Article on revolt curbs Oscar's guessing

indicators.note: to curb is to restrain or hem in, so the earlier letters enclose the phonetic letter

blocks.note: the definite article
a rising is a rebellion
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A news piece on an uprising restricts the Academy Award winner's speculation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' just means placed next to here, and the 's stands for 'is', a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Theorising is forming ideas without proof, which amounts to guessing.

clue.text: Pacemaker out of the running

blocks.note: first meaning: one who makes paces, a walker
second meaning: not running, so walking, or dull and uninspired

explanation.walkthrough: A pacemaker usually sets the speed in a race or keeps a heart beating; here it is literally someone making paces on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestrian walks rather than runs, and as an adjective the word means plodding and unremarkable.

clue.text: Dance company from hell?

blocks.note: Dis is the classical underworld
Co is short for company

explanation.surface: A dance troupe straight out of the inferno.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a party or club where people dance to recorded pop music.

clue.text: Make desert of?

blocks.note: surface reading: turn some place into a barren waste
setter's reading: 'desert' split as DE plus a word for woodland; taking away the trees is what makes a desert of the land

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the word-play: desert as a verb is to abandon, but clearing woodland creates desert.
explanation.definitionFit: To deforest land is to strip it of trees, which can leave it barren.

clue.text: Channel swimmer's not beginning to sink

indicators.note: without a beginning means the swimmer's name loses its first letter

blocks.note: Captain Matthew Webb first swam the English Channel in 1875

explanation.surface: A cross-Channel swimmer is not fit to start, and might go under.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel is the English Channel between England and France.
explanation.definitionFit: To ebb is to decline or recede, as the tide does, so it means sink in that sense.

clue.text: Former cost of education?

indicators.note: taken out of a longer word, so the answer is drawn from inside it

blocks.note: the letters sitting inside the word

explanation.surface: A wistful question about what schooling used to cost.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the trick: the old coin is literally contained in the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A ducat was a gold coin used in Europe for centuries, a historical unit of money paid out.

clue.text: Magnetism makes cleaner mum?

blocks.note: a char, or charwoman, is a cleaning lady
makes in the sense of 'two and two makes four'
Ma is a word for mother

explanation.surface: The attraction in the home is that the cleaner becomes the mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is personal magnetism, a compelling charm that draws people in.

clue.text: Fresh debate could produce support for kippers

definitions.note: the answer is plural; support is taken collectively

indicators.note: to produce something new from material implies reworking it into another arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Renewed argument might yield a defence of smoked herring.
explanation.walkthrough: A kipper here is a sleeper: kip is British slang for sleep, not the smoked fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Featherbeds are soft mattresses that hold up people taking a nap.

clue.text: Flavours of recipes initially repressed by backward Pacific nation

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of the cooking word is kept
backward means the island state is spelt in reverse
something repressed is held down within, so it sits inside the other word

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
Samoa is an island country in the Pacific

explanation.surface: An undeveloped island nation stifles the tastes of its traditional dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: SAMOA reversed is AOMAS, with R placed inside after the first A.
explanation.definitionFit: Aromas are smells, especially of food, closely tied to flavour.

clue.text: Listen to the audience in Hackney or Bow

indicators.note: what hearers in a Cockney district catch is the dialect pronunciation, dropping the h

blocks.note: hark means listen, said without its H in Cockney speech

explanation.surface: A call for attention to listeners in two parts of East London.
explanation.walkthrough: Hackney and Bow are East London districts; Cockney speech drops the initial H, so hark becomes 'ark. Bow looks like a place, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc is a curve, the same shape as a bow.

clue.text: Pat's lacking wheels, as learner's driven off

indicators.note: driven off means gone away, so the learner's letter is removed

blocks.note: without a car
L for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: Pat has no car since the learner has taken it away.
explanation.walkthrough: Pat looks like a name; it is the verb for a light touch.
explanation.definitionFit: To caress is to stroke gently, much like a pat, a soft touch of the hand.

clue.text: SHAPE runs unit moving leader east by public transport

indicators.note: the first letter is shifted rightwards one place, a small rearrangement of the word for unit

blocks.note: R stands for runs in cricket scores
the ohm is the unit of electrical resistance
a bus is public transport

explanation.surface: SHAPE, a military headquarters, operates a unit that moves its commander east by bus.
explanation.walkthrough: OHM's first letter moves one place to the right (east, in an across light) to give HOM. SHAPE is NATO's Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhombus is a geometric figure with four equal sides, an example of a shape.

clue.text: Pointed remark that's wasted on doll

indicators.note: something wasted is lost, so the abbreviation for 'that is' disappears from the toy

blocks.note: i.e. stands for id est, 'that is'
Barbie is the famous fashion doll

explanation.surface: A cutting comment was lost on a doll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' reads as 'that is', abbreviated IE, which comes out of BARBIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A barb is a cutting or hurtful remark, named after the sharp point of a hook.

clue.text: British haulier initially missing roadblock?

indicators.note: initially missing means the word loses its opening letter

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
a carrier is a haulage firm

explanation.surface: A UK freight firm's lorry has gone astray at a road closure.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: a roadblock is one kind of barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrier is any obstruction, and a roadblock is one set up across a road.

clue.text: Shrub right out in the wild?

indicators.note: out means taken away, so the letter for right leaves the word for scrubby plants

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
brush is shrubby undergrowth, brushwood

explanation.surface: Is a shrub right at home out in the wilderness?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrub' wants to be the definition, but it is the wordplay: BRUSH loses its R.
explanation.definitionFit: The bush is wild, uncultivated country, especially in Australia or Africa, far from towns.

clue.text: Hollywood dancer's boundless steps

definitions.note: a stair can mean a whole flight of steps

indicators.note: without bounds means the name loses its outer letters at both edges

blocks.note: Fred Astaire, the film dancer

explanation.surface: A film star's dance steps are unlimited.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair, or a flight of stairs, is a series of steps between floors.

clue.text: Nasty muggers (not German) suffering ocular defect

indicators.note: not here means without, so the abbreviation for that nationality is removed
suffering suggests the letters are knocked about into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
Ger is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: Vicious street robbers, not from Germany, have a problem with their eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: Take GER out of NASTY MUGGERS and rearrange the remaining nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nystagmus is a medical condition of involuntary, rapid eye movement, an example of an eye disorder.
